title: Merge companion: no filing path when the post-merge build fails
description:
The merge companion gives no filing path when the post-merge build fails.

Evidence at b75bc2f: skills/pr-with-codex-bot-review-merge/SKILL.md:211 runs nix build with no failure branch, and :218-220 starts filing only "After the successful post-merge build". If that build fails, nothing says whether or when the PR's Follow-ups get filed.

Raised by: a PR #116 review thread (PRRT_kwDORvrQys62e7n3, on skills/pr-with-codex-bot-review-merge/SKILL.md:219, rated Minor). Rated P2: a real gap in a procedure an agent follows. Not higher: an edge beyond the brief (a merged PR whose base then fails nix build), and nothing is lost, because the list stays in the merged PR's body and can be filed once the base builds.

Smallest fix: say that when the post-merge build fails, the filing step still runs once the base is repaired (or from the merged base commit anyway), and that the report names the pending list.

Verify: read the companion; a failed build leaves a named, reachable filing step.

Source: the severity-policy change, PR #116 (https://github.com/douglaz/skills/pull/116, merged as b75bc2f), rloop Run 20261112T042907.961273566Z-730464. First seen in the Run at f53ea71 (PR #116 first commit); re-checked at b75bc2f, where it still holds.

title: Bead audit: separate its own metadata writes from post-audit graph mutations
description:
The bead audit's permitted metadata writes (follow-up comments and nit beads) are not clearly separated from the polishing rule that any graph mutation after an audit invalidates its verdict.

Evidence at b75bc2f:
- skills/second-model-bead-audit/SKILL.md:44-46: "the permitted follow-up comments and nit beads record the audit without requiring re-audit."
- skills/second-model-bead-audit/SKILL.md:233-247: the finish writes those comments and nit beads.
- skills/bead-polish-loop/SKILL.md:200-201: "Any graph mutation after an audit invalidates that verdict and requires a new panel snapshot."

Raised by: two Run Reviewers (rated P1 and P2). Rated P3: no requirement needs changing; the two texts can be reconciled as written, and the problem is confusing wording.

Smallest fix: say that the permitted metadata writes finish within the audit, before its result returns; later graph mutation stays under the polishing rule.

Verify: read the audit's finish/synthesis order and the polishing handoff together; no permission, verdict or re-audit requirement changes.

Source: the severity-policy change, PR #116 (https://github.com/douglaz/skills/pull/116, merged as b75bc2f), rloop Run 20261112T042907.961273566Z-730464. First seen in the Run at f53ea71 (PR #116 first commit); re-checked at b75bc2f, where it still holds.

title: Selective installs may omit the filing steps' rule references and beads-jsonl-path
description:
Selective installs may omit the files that the new follow-up filing steps load.

Evidence at b75bc2f: install.sh:110-127 (companion_dependencies) has no entries for the filing loads added by PR #116:
- skills/pr-with-codex-bot-review-merge/SKILL.md:223 links ../multi-reviewer-loop/references/disposition-rules.md#filing-follow-ups, and :231 loads beads-jsonl-path;
- skills/second-model-bead-audit/SKILL.md:225 links the disposition-rules severity rubric, and :245 loads beads-jsonl-path;
- skills/delegate-to-manager/references/manager-brief-template.md:157 links the same disposition rules.
A selective install of one of these skills without multi-reviewer-loop or beads-jsonl-path leaves those links unresolved.

Raised by: two Run Reviewers. Rated P2: a real installation edge outside PR #116's allowed file set. Not higher: full installs carry every skill, some of these dependencies already existed at the base, and the merge companion restates the core rules inline. Found by reading; no real selective install was run.

Smallest fix: in an installer change, make selective installs of the affected skills also install beads-jsonl-path and the multi-reviewer-loop rule references they link.

Verify: isolated selective-install fixtures (install.test) resolve every filing resource each affected skill links, without touching real installed skills.

Source: the severity-policy change, PR #116 (https://github.com/douglaz/skills/pull/116, merged as b75bc2f), rloop Run 20261112T042907.961273566Z-730464. First seen in the Run at f53ea71 (PR #116 first commit); re-checked at b75bc2f, where it still holds.

title: Skeptical-audit cut descriptions overstate their remaining use
description:
The skeptical audit's generic cut descriptions overstate what cuts are still for.

Evidence at b75bc2f:
- skills/multi-reviewer-loop/SKILL.md:876-878 ("over-specification. Run § 4a and cut") and :905-911 (CUT / SIMPLIFY / MARK-OPTIONAL);
- skills/multi-reviewer-loop/references/reviewer-panel.md:736-745 (the audit prompt asks to flag anything that "could be cut, simplified, or deferred");
- against skills/multi-reviewer-loop/references/disposition-rules.md:271-273 and SKILL.md:923-925, which apply cuts only to introduced or brief-blocking P0/P1 remedies and FILE P2/P3.

Raised by: two Run Reviewers (one rated P2, one asked it as a question). Rated P3: the explicit disposition rules already scope simplification to P0/P1 remedies; the remaining problem is prose.

Smallest fix: tighten the generic cut descriptions to say they simplify a P0/P1 remedy, and that lower-severity findings and suggestions are listed for follow-up.

Verify: read § 4a and its prompt against the disposition rules; the over-specification test and the no-repair rule for P2/P3 are unchanged.
